It was submitted before the Court on the last date of hearing that the private parties have already settled the disputes amicably in both the matters and have executed the compromise deeds, copies whereof are placed on the record of the files.

2. Perused the record of two files exhaustively and also heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3.

It is submitted by the private parties present in person before the Court that they have resolved their disputes amicably and as such, accordingly want quashment of FIR bearing No.167/2019 dated 19.11.2019 of Police Station, Nowabad, Jammu, impugned in CRM(M) No. 455/2021 and setting aside 2025:JKLHC-JMU:4499 of the judgment and decree dated 18.12.2024 passed by the Court of learned Additional Principal Judge (Family Court), Jammu by declaring the marriage between them as a nullity in terms of the provisions of Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

sentences.text: Through the medium of the petition CRM(M) No. 455/2021, the petitioner therein has sought the quashment of the FIR bearing No. 167/2019 dated 19.11.2019 of Police Station, Nowabad, Jammu on the main grounds that the same is outcome of a totally false and frivolous complaint leveling allegation of commission of rape against him.
That actually the private respondent/complainant married to him while concealing her earlier existing marriage.
That the police concerned without conducting a preliminary enquiry registered the FIR.
That the private respondent/complainant executed a marriage agreement dated 12.09.2019 by putting him under pressure.
That the complainant/respondent No.2 under love affair compelled him to execute a marriage agreement with her.
That despite solemnizing marriage with him, the complainant/respondent No.2 did not maintain physical relation with him and she simply continued to threaten and blackmail him so as to extract money.
That he also challenged the validity of the marriage dated 13.09.2019 which came to be contracted between the complainant/respondent No.2 and him under concealment of fats.
That he never maintained any physical relation with respondent No.2/ complainant.

5. By way of the Regular First Appeal No. 2/2025, the petitioner has sought setting aside of the judgment and decree dated 18.12.2024 passed by the Court of learned Additional Principal Judge (Family Court), Jammu on a petition under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act filed by him titled 2025:JKLHC-JMU:4499 "Naresh Kumar vs Mohini Devi", File No. 593/2019, by virtue of which,
the learned trial Court dismissed his petition.

It is the case of the appellant that he approached the learned trial Court through a petition in terms of Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act seeking declaration of his marriage with respondent as null and void as being in violation of the provisions of Section 5 of the Act, but the learned trial Court dismissed his petition on illegal and unjustified ground that since he was in know of the fact of the earlier existing marriage of the respondent with one Pritam Lal, as such, he is estoppel to take recourse to provisions of Section 11 of the Act for declaring the marriage as null and void.
6.
Since the private parties have now mutually compromised in respect of both the matters and have also placed on record of both the files the copies of compromise.
Their statements in proof of their mutual settlement stand recorded.

7. In the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it may meet the ends of justice and will also be in accordance with the law in case both the matters are allowed on the basis of a mutual settlement between the private parties.

The quashment of the FIR impugned in the criminal petition bearing CRM(M) No. 455/2021 will facilitate the private parties to settle their future life as per their own choice as they have mutually settled to separate from each other.

The judgment and decree dated 18.12.2024 of the learned Additional Principal Judge (Family Court),
Jammu otherwise appears to be suffering from illegality as the learned trial Court despite recording his satisfaction that the private parties had executed marriage during the subsisting marriage of the respondent Mohini Devi with Pritam Lal, did not allow the petition under Section 11 of the Hindu 2025:JKLHC-JMU:4499 Marriage Act thereby legalizing an illegality.

It was brought on record of the proceedings before the learned trial Court that the parties to the appeal purportedly solemnized the marriage on 13.09.2019 at Arya Samaj Mandir Janipur Colony, Jammu when the first marriage of the respondent Mohini Devi with her earlier husband Pritam Lal came to be dissolved through the judgment and decree dated 06.09.2021 passed by the Court of learned Additional Principal Judge Naresh Kumar vs Ut Of J&K & Anr on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152547693/
2 (Family Court), Jammu.

sentences.text: Although this Court is of the opinion that an FIR cannot be generally and in routine manner allowed to be quashed in exercise of the powers under Section 528 of BNSS corresponding to Section 482 of the Code on the main ground that the parties have settled their controversy that had become the cause of occurrence, yet exceptional ground appears to be made out in the opinion of the Court, in the facts and the circumstances of the case, for invoking its extraordinary powers under Section 528 of BNSS to quash the FIR in question.

9. The provisions of Section 359 of the BNSS corresponding to Section 320 of the Code do not restrict but limit and circumvent the powers of this Court under Section 528 of the BNSS corresponding to Section 482 of the Code regarding quashment of FIR's and criminal proceedings for the sake of the society at large which is real beneficiary of the criminal justice delivery system.

10. This Court in its opinion feels fortified with an authoritative judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court cited as "Gopal Kumar B. Nar Vs. CBI (2014) 5 SCC 800" in which it has been held that "though quashment of non- compoundable offence under Section 482 CrPC, following a settlement between the parties would not amount to circumvention of Section 320, but 2025:JKLHC-JMU:4499 such power has to be exercised with care and caution and would depend on facts of each case."

(2017) 9 SCC 641" has considered the aspect of the invocation of the inherent powers by the High Courts under Section 528 of the BNSS corresponding to Section 482 of the Code and was pleased to lay down some broad governing principles for invocation of such power of the High Courts.

The relevant portions of the judgment are reproduced as under for the sake of convenience:
"Section 482 is prefaced with an overriding provision.

The statute saves the inherent power of the High Court, as a superior court, to make such orders as are necessary (i)
to prevent an abuse of the process of any court; or (ii) otherwise to secure the ends of justice.

The broad principles which emerge from the precedents on the subject, may be summarised in the following propositions:
(i) Section 482 preserves the inherent powers of the High Court to prevent an abuse of the process of any court or to secure the ends of justice.
The provision does not confer new powers.

It only recognises and preserves powers which inhere in the High Court;
(ii) The invocation of the jurisdiction of the High Court to quash a First Information Report or a criminal proceeding on the ground that a settlement has been arrived at between the offender and the victim is not the same as the invocation of jurisdiction for the purpose of compounding an offence.

While compounding an offence, the Naresh Kumar vs Ut Of J&K & Anr on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152547693/
3 power of the court is governed by the provisions of Section 320 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

sentences.text: The power to quash under Section 482 is attracted even if the offence is non- compoundable.

(iii) In forming an opinion whether a criminal proceeding or complaint should be quashed in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482, the High Court must evaluate whether the ends of justice would justify the exercise of the inherent power;
(iv) While the inherent power of the High Court has a 2025:JKLHC-JMU:4499 wide ambit and plenitude it has to be exercised; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent an abuse of the process of any court;

(v) The decision as to whether a complaint or First Information Report should be quashed on the ground that the offender and victim have settled the dispute, revolves ultimately on the facts and circumstances of each case and no exhaustive elaboration of principles can be formulated;
(vi) In the exercise of the power under Section 482 and while dealing with a plea that the dispute has been settled, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the offence.

Heinous and serious offences involving mental depravity or offences such as murder, rape and dacoity cannot appropriately be quashed though the victim or the family of the victim have settled the dispute.
Such offences are, truly speaking, not private in nature but have a serious impact upon society.
The decision to continue with the trial in such cases is founded on the overriding element of public interest in punishing persons for serious offences;
(vii) As distinguished from serious offences, there may be criminal cases which have an overwhelming or predominant element of a civil dispute.
Economic offences involving the financial and economic well-being of the state have implications which lie beyond the domain of a mere dispute between private disputants.
The High Court would be justified in declining to quash where the offender is involved in an activity akin to a financial or economic fraud or misdemeanour.

High Court is not foreclosed from examining as to whether there exists material for incorporation of such offences or as to whether there is sufficient evidence which if proved would lead to proving for offence charged with.
iii. Court has also to take into consideration as to whether settlement between the parties is going to result in harmony between them which may improve their mutual relationship.
iv. It is also relevant to consider as to what is the stage of proceedings.

If application (for quashing proceedings) is made at belated stage wherein evidence has been led and matter is at stage of arguments or judgment, Court should be slow to exercise power to quash proceedings.
However, if such application is made at initial stage before commencement of trial, said factor will weight with Court in exercising its power.
v. In present case, facts and circumstances are peculiar.
Respondent 2 is young lady of 23 years.

She feels that going through trial in one case, where she is complainant,
and in other case, wherein she is accused, would rob prime of her youth.
She feels that if she is made to face trial rather than getting any relief, she would be faced with agony of undergoing trial.
vi. In both aforesaid cases, though charge-sheets have been filed, charges are yet to be framed and as such, trial has not yet commenced.
It is further to be noted that since Respondent 2 herself is not supporting prosecution case, even if criminal trial is permitted to go ahead, it will end in nothing else than acquittal.
If request of parties is denied, it will be amounting to only adding one more criminal case already overburdened criminal courts.

sentences.text: Such an approach is likely to put an end to some further apprehended litigation of both civil and criminal nature and to allow the parties to have a peaceful and cordial relation, besides saving the precious time of the Criminal Courts being already grossly over-burdened as the continuance of such criminal proceedings is likely to prove a futile exercise only for the purpose of completing the procedure for recording an order of acquittal at the end.

Provisions of Section 320 of the Code corresponding to Section 359 of the BNSS do not restrict but only limit the powers of this Court under Section 482 of the Code corresponding to Section 528 of BNSS so that the extraordinary powers are used only in exceptional circumstances to meet the ends of justice.
Provisions of Section 482 of the Code (528 of BNSS) have an overriding affect and are not to be read as subject to the provisions of Section 320 of the Code (359 of BNSS).

The criminal proceedings, involving heinous offences of anti- social nature or offences under special penal statutes do not qualify for being quashed/compounded in exercise of the powers under Section 482 of the Code (528 BNSS).
17. Criminal litigation between neighbours, near relatives or co-sharers more often originates from the civil/matrimonial disputes and as such directing the quashment of proceedings by invoking the inherent powers under the Code/BNSS, in such matters of personal nature not involving the commission of any heinous offence is likely to meet the ends of justice.
18.

Setting aside of the impugned judgment and decree dated 18.12.2024 of the learned Additional Principal Judge (Family Court), Jammu, is otherwise warranted under law, having regard to the facts and the circumstances of the case.
19. In the backdrop, both the matters are allowed.

20. By allowing the petition filed under the provisions of Section 482 of CrPC corresponding to Section 528 of BNSS, the impugned case FIR bearing No.167/2019 dated 19.11.2019 under Section 376 IPC of Police Station, Nowabad Jammu, is hereby quashed.

21. By allowing of the Regular First Appeal bearing No. 2/2025, the judgment and decree dated 18.12.2024 passed by the Court of learned Additional Principal Judge (Family Court), Jammu is set aside and the marriage between the appellant and the respondent is declared as null and void as being in contravention of the provisions of Section 5(1) of the Hindu Marriages Act.
